maturity.title: Current maturity
maturity.body: Moriarty Webs is a concept under review. Supplied records include one current-Rust invoice-partial Groth16 roundtrip (S07) and seven finite local compiled-C2-wrapper cases (S08: one acceptance and six mutation rejections), with a single-party test setup whose operator can forge proofs and caller-fabricated proof contexts. No on-chain transaction is recorded. Only a conditional lowering argument is adopted. V2 consumer descriptions on this page are Opus readings of unadopted, uncompiled source, not observed behavior or exact-source correspondence to those runs. General Web integration, genuine intent authorization, onchain settlement and all-family compatibility remain unestablished in this packet. Local VM cost is not ledger cost. Every interactive example on this page is an illustration.

cards.title: What a verifying proof shows
cards.body: Under an honest setup and Groth16 knowledge soundness, a verifying proof shows the prover knew a witness satisfying the compiled constraints for its two public inputs. Linking those inputs to statement bytes additionally rests on the in-circuit BLAKE2b gadget and on BLAKE2b collision resistance. It never authenticates those bytes. A proof over supplied values does not make them an authenticated ledger fact or a true outside observation. A concrete execution proof, a universal property certificate and an authenticated ledger claim are different assertions; the latter two are not established Strand kinds.
assumptions: The current class-0 test setup is forgeable by its operator, so no production security claim follows.
Whether the compiled constraints and verifying key match your source is OPEN (T3: compiled circuit/VK and BLAKE2b gadget correspondence).
Outside facts keep their named issuer, predicate, authentication path and freshness limits.

Reference-input reads are PROPOSED: the validator must read the datum itself and authenticate its origin. PREMISE: being unspent at application shows presence only, with no exclusivity or history. A validity interval neither dates nor authenticates a datum.

SEC06-P06 PROPOSED; still needs real-context stale-sequence and expired-attestation cases, changed-reference-datum and forged-origin negatives, N5/N7–N9 at V, and a separately scoped real-context proof.

cards.title: Setup and keys
cards.body: The current test setup can be forged by its operator; whether the verifying key matches the compiled relation is OPEN. Groth16 needs a separate setup per distinct compiled circuit (R1CS matrices), not per logical predicate. In the current Rust source the predicate digest is a circuit constant, so each distinct relation identity is a distinct circuit. The required total setup count is unknown; predicate, catalogue and family counts do not determine it. No production ceremony is recorded in the supplied sources, and none is proposed here.
assumptions: A future universal circuit or Midnight's universal PLONK/KZG SRS would change the comparison (PROPOSED or target-specific).

V2 SOURCE READING: catalogue VK digests are fixed at genesis and carried unchanged, and Close requires zero balances and duties, so any key change needs a PROPOSED key migration action that carries residual duties.
Intent revocation (Revoke) advances seq; it is not key migration.
SEC06-P07 PROPOSED; still needs an old-VK-refused-after-migration negative, a setup-class report and independent review of any future ceremony.
cards.evidenceStage: RECORDED limitation (forgeable test setup); V2 SOURCE READING; total setup count UNKNOWN

cards.title: What ties a Strand to its step
cards.body: V2 SOURCE READING: tag, family, predicate_digest, shape_digest and body_len are circuit constants; the context fields vk_digest through intents_digest (bytes 112..339, including claimant_vkh) are free booleanized witness bits that are hashed, not interpreted. The consumer, not the circuit, ties those fields to the transaction: the settling validator rebuilds each statement from the transaction and the spent thread state, so a claim made for another thread step, catalogue, claimant or intent set does not match. Claimant binding happens at consumption, not at issuance: C2 Issue does not compare the claimant with the statement, so a mismatched envelope can be minted but cannot settle. This source-level binding is separate from T3, which stays OPEN.
assumptions: The class-0 setup operator can forge a proof for any digest and any claimant. The claimant is prover-chosen bytes, not an authenticated prover identity.
Builders select claim inputs; the ledger spends each claim once (PREMISE). A copied proof can be re-issued with the same claimant and a new expiry; only that claimant can release it.

Catalogue program_hash and source_hash are visible, covered by catalogue_digest and signed in every owner intent. No on-chain check links them to predicate_digest or vk_digest: that link is a CATALOGUE-AUTHOR ASSERTION and VK-to-matrix is OPEN. Exact predicate-digest field coverage depends on identity.rs, which the reviewer did not read.
The statement's network byte is declared by the catalogue and not compared with the executing ledger; separation across networks rests on outref uniqueness (PREMISE).

SEC06-P03 and SEC06-P04 PROPOSED; still need competing-claimant and same-claimant duplicate negatives, second-party source→relation→predicate reproduction, refusal-list coverage, N5/N7–N9, a T3 method, reviewed T2/T3 and F07–F10, a non-test setup, and cross-network replay analysis if the network byte is relied on.
cards.evidenceStage: V2 SOURCE READING (unadopted, uncompiled); T3 OPEN

cards.title: Where proofs are checked: the issuance route
cards.body: In the reviewed V2 source, each proof is checked when its claim is issued: the C2 claim policy checks a Groth16 proof and mints one claim output per Issue transaction. Claims must exist before settlement. The settlement transaction consumes them, recomputes each statement and compares it with the digest checked at issuance; it does not verify the proof again. Each consumed claim needs its claimant's signature on the settlement transaction and the burn of its token. Structurally, n required Strands mean n Issue transactions plus one settlement, excluding one-time genesis and any post-expiry reclaim. These counts are readings of uncompiled source, not measurements.
assumptions: Each claim output locks min-ADA from issuance until settlement or claimant-signed reclaim after the claimant-chosen expiry. Several envelopes can exist per statement digest.

Safe but not live: any catalogue account may Revoke (advancing seq), and a competing settlement may spend the outref, orphaning issued claims and locking their value until expiry. Earlier reclaim is PROPOSED (OPEN).

Batch issuance needs a C2 change (PROPOSED). Proof-at-consumption is a different PROPOSED design needing a new redeemer and in-settlement pairings, with size and budget unmeasured. Mempool chaining is a node premise outside the sources.
V2 source already refuses two claims for one consumed outref; S09's role-level refusal is an unadopted proposal and not deduplication permission.
Owner intents are signed before proving; claimant settlement signatures are a later, distinct event. Proof collection or claim-output creation executes no effect.
Still needs orphan-after-Revoke, competing-settlement and post-expiry reclaim cases, and a qualified complete-path measurement of both verification placements.
cards.evidenceStage: V2 SOURCE READING (structural); not observed onchain

cards.title: Complete and incomplete Webs
cards.body: PROPOSED: a Web settles only when every Strand its contract requires is present. An incomplete Web has no authority over thread effects. On the issuance route its already-issued claim outputs exist on-chain, lock value, and remain releasable only by their claimant. In the first proposed supported profile, the consumer refuses universal property certificates, authenticated-history claims, private handoff, recursive parents and multiparent joins as UNSUPPORTED; they remain required Web tracks, each needing its own trust path and evidence before any profile accepts it.
assumptions: All-or-nothing acceptance and a consumer-derived required set are PROPOSED; no Web consumer, second genuine relation or general cardinality exists in this packet.

Depicting several Strand roles does not establish separate relations or producers. A whole-execution proof may cover several claim specifications; naming source expressions fee or liability does not create independent proof producers.

A01 adopts only conditional T1: the all-role conjunction equals whole-action Core over one decoded body, modulo premise G including output well-formedness, a covering WebPlan, whole-action compilation first and the same field. There is no implementation, no T2, no T3 and no full WP migration (F07–F10); builder reliance is not permitted.
OPEN: whether a consumer can enforce a fully authorized partial financial step that carries every proof that step requires, distinct from a missing proof.

SEC06-P01 and SEC06-P02 PROPOSED; still need N1/N12 and unknown-class refusal, a report-level test that an incomplete set never renders as accepted, N1–N4/N6/N11/N14 at H/V, a wrong-action-index case, a required-set display, separate future-profile designs and fresh security review of reused V2 mechanisms.

cards.title: Effects, allocation and authority
cards.body: V2 SOURCE READING: owner intents sign per-asset gross_cap, fee_cap, net_floor and liability_cap for a beneficiary, a validity window, nonce = seq and the target predicate, VK and shape digests. Duties change only through recorded accruals and discharges, and a thread with a nonzero duty cannot close. The thread datum carries the complete custody snapshot, which custody must equal exactly. Actual output allocation is the consuming validator's job; a proof can attest arithmetic only over values the validator recomputes. A profile chooses either strict one-output-per-obligation or a consumer-recomputed amount partition that admits coalesced payments, with every obligation allocated exactly once.
assumptions: The source strict-output rule covers redeemers of one S2 script hash only, not other scripts or S2 versions. No input value may count toward two obligations; ledger single-spend alone is not a value partition.
Circuit-level NotBound/TouchedOnly limits remain. A general multi-UTxO authenticated frame, role sets, cross-script allocation and partial-completion rules are PROPOSED.
No genuine intent signature is observed in the supplied proof records.

A supplied approved=true is consented to by the effect-derived required signers, and by a listed advancer if any; that is the debited account's consent, not a separate governance decision. A distinct approver must be a required signer, an advancer or an authenticated input.

SEC06-P05 PROPOSED; still needs double-satisfaction negatives across scripts and S2 versions, a coalesced positive under partition, fee-over-cap and dropped-duty cases, the approver-coverage lint, a genuine validator-checked signature in real context, and independent custody/duty/backing accounting with a backing-policy negative.
cards.evidenceStage: V2 SOURCE READING; allocation policy PROPOSED per profile

cards.title: Duties, backing and fees
cards.body: S12 and S13 source behavior requires non-negative custody, not full backing of liabilities. S12 funds escrow at 110: partial(35) debits 37 and leaves 73 against duties of 75 (invoice 65, reserve 10), which is 2 short. Funding 112 would back one partial; each further partial charges another 2 that no duty reflects. That backing is a PROPOSED application policy. S12 has no extra transfer and no reserve-duty-return action; after finish, escrow holds 8 against reserve duty 10, and the nonzero reserve duty blocks V2 Close. S13 allocate(true,23,7,2) needs at least 23 A and 4 B for non-negative custody; 25 A and 10 B is PROPOSED full backing, and S13 has no action discharging allocation_reserve.
assumptions: Source-only arithmetic, not execution. The V2 Close zero-duty condition is an uncompiled-source reading.
Even under the proposed 112 policy the reserve duty stays 10 and Close stays blocked; discharge or migration needs a program change.
S13 units is checked only arithmetically (23 = 3×7 + 2) and is never debited.

A program-asset fee is not debt repayment and not a network fee. Network fees, collateral, claim-output min-ADA and the V2 thread reserve (lovelace returned on Close) are separate funding items; a reserve duty is a program liability.
Delivery evidence and dispute rules remain named assumptions. Still needs independent open/partial/finish/reserve-return accounting and a backing-policy negative.

glossaryClarifications.clarification: An individual proof with its claim, statement and binding metadata. Before a proof exists, say requirement or planned proof. A signed owner intent, UTxO, claim output, validator, catalogue entry, pattern or predicate is not a Strand.

PROPOSED: the contract-fixed set of required Strands for one transition, accepted all-or-nothing by the consuming validator in a supported profile. Profiles refuse unsupported classes; certificates, authenticated history, private handoff, recursion and bounded multiparent remain required future tracks.
The reusable type of a Strand; not itself a proof. Reusing a specification does not reuse a proof for changed state.
V2 SOURCE READING: a C2 UTxO holding one token named H(envelope), minted after the claim policy's Groth16 check. It confers no authority by itself and is neither the proof nor its validator.
Issuance is the reviewed V2 route. Verification at consumption is PROPOSED and needs a new redeemer and in-settlement pairings.
Thread reserve is V2 lovelace returned on Close. A reserve duty is a program liability such as S12 reserve or S13 allocation_reserve.
Revoke advances seq to cancel outstanding intents and can orphan issued claims. Key migration (VK change) is PROPOSED; V2 catalogues are immutable.
A per-profile choice between strict one-output-per-obligation (reviewed V2 scope: one S2 script hash) and a consumer-recomputed amount partition.
thread is a V2 source identifier for the consumer's state instance (thread id, thread effects, thread reserve). It is not a public synonym for Strand; public vocabulary is Web and Strand.
ILLUSTRATION: every illustrated requirement has an illustrated Strand. It is not proof verification, acceptance or settlement.
Actual target-ledger acceptance of the authorized effects under the applicable conditions. Nothing on this page settles anything.
A link stated by the catalogue author and not checked on-chain, here between program_hash/source_hash and predicate_digest/vk_digest.
A Cardano ledger rule assumed by the reasoning but not contained in the sources, for example single spending of an outref.

A connection from a Strand to its consumer means required by (PROPOSED). Do not label it verifies, executes or triggers, and do not depict automatic output triggering, chaining, aggregation, recursion or batching.

Issuance-route diagram order: owner intents signed → proof production → one Issue per Strand (C2 checks the proof, mints one claim output, locks min-ADA) → one settlement (consumes claim outputs, recomputes statements against the issuance-checked digest, each claimant signs, tokens burned) → separate observation of inclusion, finality and readback. No freshness badge from a validity interval, no network-authentication badge from the catalogue network byte, and the claimant shown as prover-chosen bytes, not an authenticated identity.

Financial partial progress (a duty remaining) and a missing required proof are separate states with separate controls. The invoice worksheet never changes Web completeness, and no proof badge appears in the worksheet.
Every security-relevant state (incomplete, illustrative assembled, PROPOSED, OPEN, recorded) is conveyed in text, not by color or motion alone.

invoiceRules.rule: Opening is a source reading, not an executed result: S12 open(90,10) gives invoice duty 100 (face = 90 + 10), reserve duty 10 and escrow 110 CASH. The buyer pays the 110 transfer plus a 3 CASH program-asset fee, a gross debit of 113. CASH is the S12 fixture asset (network oracle-unit), not a Cardano asset.
Slider domain: integers 1 to 99 inclusive. S12 partial requires amount > 0 and amount < opening, and opening is 100.

0 and 100 are refusals, not accepted source actions. If shown as test cases, label them Refused: requires amount > 0, and Refused: requires amount < opening (100). Paying the whole balance is the separate finish action, which charges no fee and is not part of this one-partial worksheet.

Source behavior (S12, not executed): escrow debit = amount + 2; escrow cash = 110 − amount − 2; invoice duty = 100 − amount; reserve duty = 10; total duties = 110 − amount. After one partial the source path is always 2 short of total duties. Example amount 35: debit 37, cash 73, duties 65 + 10 = 75. Never label this path fully backed.

PROPOSED full-backing view: funding 112, cash = 112 − amount − 2, which equals total duties after one partial. Label it PROPOSED application policy. S12 open funds exactly face + reserve and has no extra transfer, so 112 is not an S12 action, and the source enforces only non-negative custody, not backing.
Funding 112 backs one partial only. Each further partial charges escrow another 2 that no duty reflects, so later fees create further gaps unless a further rule and funding are adopted.

The 2 CASH fee goes to fees and is not debt repayment; the invoice duty falls only by the payment amount. Network fees, collateral, claim-output min-ADA and the V2 thread reserve are separate, unknown here and not included in the worksheet.

Reserve: S12 has no reserve-duty-return action, so reserve duty 10 remains. If finish is mentioned, the source path leaves cash 8 against reserve duty 10 (the proposed 112 path leaves 10 against 10), and the nonzero reserve duty blocks V2 Close either way. Never show closed, complete or reserve returned.

The worksheet is a local arithmetic lesson. It does not execute Moriarty or a proof and creates no transaction or ledger state. A permitted partial step is intended to carry every proof required for that step (PROPOSED; consumer enforcement OPEN); remaining duty is not a missing proof.
Required visible labels: Source behavior (S12, not executed) and PROPOSED full-backing policy, plus the explicit 2-short line on the source path.

main.heroBody: Moriarty is a language for financial contracts. Webs let a Cardano application attach proofs to a transaction, so its validator can check that the contract’s rules were followed.
main.explorerIntro: An invoice is one use for a Web. Choose another application to see the conditions its contract checks. Select a condition to read the claim and where its inputs come from; remove proof coverage for it to see why an incomplete set cannot settle.
main.proofRoleExplanation: A condition is something the contract requires, such as a correct fee calculation. A Strand contains a Groth16 proof, its public claim and the information tying it to this transaction. One proof can cover several conditions. The settlement validator rebuilds the claim from the transaction and checks that it matches the claim whose proof was verified. An external price or delivery record still needs an authenticated source and a freshness rule.

definitions.body: A Strand carries one Groth16 proof, the claim it proves and the information that ties it to a particular transaction. For an invoice, its claim might cover the payment calculation and the unpaid balance.
A Web collects the Strands a contract requires for a transaction. The contract sets those requirements. Settlement needs every required condition covered by a matching Strand.

A claim specification describes a kind of claim: what it asserts, which inputs it uses and which compiled rules it must satisfy. It can be reused across transactions; a proof for an old state cannot simply be reused for a changed one.

main.assemblyComplete: All required conditions are covered. The Web can be submitted for settlement; the validator still checks it against the actual transaction.
main.assemblyIncomplete: A required condition has no proof coverage. This Web cannot authorize settlement. Any proof claims already issued remain locked until settlement or a claimant-signed reclaim after expiry.

worksheet.title: Choose how much to pay the seller
worksheet.intro: The invoice is for 100 CASH, with a separate reserve obligation of 10 CASH. The escrow—the account holding the funds—starts with {openingCash} CASH. Each partial payment costs a 2 CASH program fee.
worksheet.modeBody: The extra 2 CASH funds the fee for this payment. Afterward, the remaining cash covers both the unpaid invoice and the reserve.
worksheet.amountRangeNote: Choose 1–99 CASH for a partial payment. Paying the full invoice uses a separate action.

rows.programFee: Program fee to the fee recipient {fee} CASH

worksheet.backingLine: The remaining {cash} CASH covers {duties} CASH still owed.
worksheet.feeRule: The {amount} CASH payment reduces the invoice balance. The separate {fee} CASH fee does not.
worksheet.oneStepNote: This example funds one partial payment. Another partial payment would need another {fee} CASH fee allowance.
worksheet.proofSeparation: A partial payment still needs all of its proofs. An unpaid balance does not make the Web incomplete.
worksheet.assetNote: CASH is an example unit in the invoice program.
worksheet.networkFeeNote: Cardano network fees, collateral and the minimum ADA held in proof-claim outputs are separate; this worksheet does not estimate them.

main.lifecycleIntro: The example uses an issuance route: proofs are checked in earlier transactions, then their on-chain claim outputs are consumed together at settlement. Creating those outputs does not execute the invoice payment.

lifecycleSteps.title: The owner signs limits
lifecycleSteps.body: Before proving, the owner signs an intent that limits what may leave the account and what each recipient must receive. It also identifies the permitted fees, validity window and proof relation. A one-time nonce prevents the same authorization being used again.

lifecycleSteps.title: A prover builds the Web
lifecycleSteps.body: The prover runs the financial program and produces the required Strands. Each claim is tied to the state being spent, its sequence number, the settlement script, the catalogue of permitted claims and verification keys, signed intents and claimant. One execution proof can cover several required conditions.

lifecycleSteps.title: Proof claims go on-chain
lifecycleSteps.body: An Issue transaction verifies one Groth16 proof and creates a claim output holding minimum ADA. This output records checked evidence for later settlement. It does not pay the seller or mint the application’s asset.

lifecycleSteps.title: The transaction settles
lifecycleSteps.body: Settlement consumes every required claim output and burns its claim token. The validator rebuilds the claims from the transaction, checks the signed limits and requires the claimants’ signatures. The application then checks inclusion and its required finality, and reads back the payments and remaining obligations.

faqs.question: Does a proof claim mint my application’s token?
faqs.answer: No. Issuing a proof claim creates an output that records checked evidence. Settlement consumes it and burns the claim token. Your application’s token has its own minting policy, which controls supply, recipients and any issuance cap.

faqs.question: Do I need permission from Moriarty to build an application?
faqs.answer: No. Developers can write, compile, prove and deploy programs in the supported language without approval from Moriarty maintainers. The application still has to follow the ledger’s rules and respect the authorization of anyone whose assets it moves. A contract may also define access rules for its own users.

faqs.question: What does the owner authorize?
faqs.answer: The owner signs an intent before proving. It defines per-asset limits on gross debits, fees and new liabilities, as well as the minimum net amount each beneficiary must receive. Its validity window, one-time nonce and exact proof relation limit where and when it can be used. Network fees are shown separately.

faqs.question: Who signs the settlement transaction?
faqs.answer: Each proof-claim output names a claimant. Consuming it at settlement requires that claimant’s signature and burns the claim token. The validator also checks the prior signed intents of the accounts being debited. Those owner authorizations and the later claimant signatures serve different purposes.

faqs.question: How do I know the payment happened?
faqs.answer: Check that the transaction was included, wait for the finality your application requires, then read back the actual outputs and remaining obligations. Reconcile those amounts with the owner’s signed intent. A timeout leaves the outcome unknown; it does not establish that the payment failed.

faqs.question: Can a partial payment have a complete Web?
faqs.answer: Yes. Completeness means every required condition for this payment has proof coverage. It does not mean the entire invoice has been paid. The unpaid invoice balance and reserve obligation remain in the next state.

faqs.question: What if the Web never settles?
faqs.answer: The issued claim outputs keep holding their minimum ADA. Their claimant can reclaim them after the chosen expiry by signing a reclaim transaction. If a catalogue account advances its sequence through revocation, or a competing settlement spends the same state, the old claims can no longer settle and must wait for expiry.

faqs.question: Does splitting a Web into more Strands reduce the cost?
faqs.answer: Each Strand needs its own Issue transaction on this route, and its claim output holds minimum ADA until settlement or reclaim. A single execution proof covering several conditions may be simpler. Comparing costs requires measuring complete transactions on the target network; splitting alone does not establish a saving.

caseCopy.summary: Pay {amount} CASH toward an invoice held in escrow. The seller receives the payment and the fee recipient receives a separate {fee} CASH. The unpaid invoice balance and reserve obligation remain in the next state.

roles.label: Payment calculation
roles.claim: The seller receives the chosen partial payment.
roles.statement: Opening invoice duty 100 CASH; payment {amount} CASH; escrow debit for payment and fee {debit} CASH.
roles.authentication: The opening duty comes from the escrow state this transition spends, and CASH is the asset the invoice program declares.

roles.label: Separate program fee
roles.claim: The escrow pays a separate {fee} CASH fee, which does not reduce the invoice balance.
roles.statement: Escrow pays the seller {amount} CASH and the fee recipient {fee} CASH; the fee does not reduce invoice duty.
roles.authentication: The consuming validator checks the actual seller and fee-recipient outputs against these amounts.

roles.label: Remaining obligations
roles.claim: The next state records the unpaid invoice balance and the unchanged reserve obligation.
roles.statement: Invoice 100 − {amount} = {invoiceDuty} CASH; reserve duty stays {reserveDuty} CASH; total duties {duties} CASH; escrow keeps {cash} CASH.
roles.authentication: Duties carry over from the spent escrow state and change only through recorded accruals and discharges.

caseCopy.summary: Exchange assets through a liquidity pool, combining two orders in one transaction. Each owner sets a minimum amount to receive. The contract must check both the pool calculation and what each owner actually receives.

roles.label: Each owner’s result
roles.claim: Each owner receives at least the minimum amount they agreed to.
roles.statement: Two orders each offer 100 A and require at least 90 B net; each owner receives 92 B.
roles.authentication: Asset identities and each owner’s limits come from the owners’ signed intents; the validator checks the actual outputs.

roles.label: Pool update
roles.claim: The updated pool reserves follow the pool’s rules for fees and rounding.
roles.statement: The reserve update, fee rule and exact rounding agree with both orders.
roles.authentication: Pool reserves come from the pool state being spent; any outside price carries its named source and freshness limit.

roles.label: Combined order accounting
roles.claim: The combined transaction accounts for both orders without counting one payment toward two orders.
roles.statement: The amounts used for each owner’s result are the amounts in the batch accounting, and no payment counts toward two orders.
roles.authentication: The consuming validator allocates actual outputs under its profile’s rule: one output per order, or an exact partition that admits combined payments with every order allocated once.

caseCopy.summary: Create 300 units of an application token under a cap of 1,000, then distribute them to two recipients. The cap leaves room for up to 700 more units under the minting policy; that capacity is not an amount already owed.

roles.label: Supply limit
roles.claim: The number of tokens issued stays within the cap.
roles.statement: First issue: 300 units under a cap of 1,000; unissued capacity is 700.
roles.authentication: The application asset’s own minting policy enforces the cap and continues the supply state from its predecessor.

roles.label: Recipient amounts
roles.claim: The amounts sent to the recipients add up to the number of tokens issued.
roles.statement: Recipient one receives 180 units and recipient two receives 120 units; 180 + 120 = 300.
roles.authentication: The minting policy and the consuming validator check the actual mint and recipient outputs.

roles.label: Separate token obligations
roles.claim: Issuing tokens creates a servicing obligation only if the program defines one.
roles.statement: The remaining 700 units of capacity are not debt. A redemption promise is a duty only when the program defines it.
roles.authentication: A servicing duty names its parties, its exact asset and its creation and discharge rules; eligibility documents keep their issuer and freshness limits.

caseCopy.summary: A debt of 100 CASH grows by 5 CASH for the period. A 35 CASH repayment reduces it to 70 CASH. The borrower also pays a 2 CASH fee, which does not repay any debt.

roles.label: Updated debt
roles.claim: The debt increases by the period’s accrued amount.
roles.statement: Debt 100 CASH plus accrual 5 CASH gives a duty of 105 CASH.
roles.authentication: The loan agreement fixes period, rate and rounding; a variable rate carries its named observation source and freshness rule.

roles.label: Repayment and fee
roles.claim: The payer funds the debt repayment and its separate fee.
roles.statement: Debt payment 35 CASH plus separate fee 2 CASH gives payer gross debit 37 CASH.
roles.authentication: Payer, lender, fee recipient and asset match the payer’s signed intent and the transaction’s actual outputs.

roles.label: Remaining debt
roles.claim: Only the repayment reduces the debt; the fee is accounted for separately.
roles.statement: Duty 105 − repayment 35 = 70 CASH remaining; the 2 CASH fee is not repayment.
roles.authentication: The continuing debt carries over from the predecessor state through explicit accrual and discharge entries; collateral release follows its own policy.

caseCopy.summary: Allocate funds to two beneficiaries while paying a separate fee. The transaction also creates reserve and rebate obligations, so the treasury must retain enough of each asset to cover them.

roles.label: Division and remainder
roles.claim: The allocation uses the correct quotient and remainder when dividing 23 by 3.
roles.statement: Dividing 23 by 3 gives 7 with a remainder of 2: 23 = 3 × 7 + 2, and the remainder is less than 3. The program call is allocate(true,23,7,2), where true supplies the approval flag.
roles.authentication: The allocation inputs, including approved=true, sit inside the intent the debited treasury account signs; a separate governance approver must itself be a required signer, an advancer or an authenticated input.

roles.label: Beneficiary payments
roles.claim: The beneficiary payments and fee match the allocation calculation.
roles.statement: Alpha receives 14 A and 4 B; beta receives 7 A; fees receive 2 A. Total custody debit is 23 A and 4 B.
roles.authentication: Treasury custody, the identities of A and B and the beneficiary outputs are checked by the consuming validator.

roles.label: Funds retained for obligations
roles.claim: The treasury keeps enough of assets A and B to cover the new reserve and rebate obligations.
roles.statement: Allocation creates a reserve duty of 2 A and a rebate duty of 6 B. The treasury holds 25 A and 10 B before the step and keeps 2 A and 6 B against those duties.
roles.authentication: Opening custody comes from the treasury state being spent; the consumer enforces that custody covers the duties.

technical.title: Implementation status and evidence
technical.summary: The page above describes Moriarty Webs as designed. This section records where the implementation stands. Supplied records include one current-Rust invoice-partial Groth16 roundtrip (S07) and seven local compiled-C2-wrapper cases (S08: one acceptance and six mutation rejections), with a single-party test setup whose operator can forge proofs and caller-fabricated proof contexts. No on-chain transaction is recorded. Descriptions of the consumer, claim policy, owner intents, duties and Close are Opus readings of unadopted, uncompiled V2 Aiken/Rust source, not observed behavior, and no supplied record pins the S07/S08 binaries or compiled bytes to that source. Of the composition argument, only conditional T1 is adopted; T2, T3 (compiled circuit/VK/BLAKE2b gadget correspondence) and the full WP migration are open. Not yet built: the all-or-nothing Web consumer and required-set enforcement, partial-step enforcement, real-context proofs, genuine intent signatures, the CLI/SDK and transaction build/submit/observe interfaces, a wallet signing display, the funding and backing actions behind the 112 CASH and 25 A / 10 B designs, reserve-duty discharge, batch issuance and any production setup ceremony. S08’s local VM figures are not ledger cost, and no cost, latency or portability advantage is measured or claimed.
technical.sourceVersusDesign: Invoice. The worksheet uses the fee-funded design: escrow opens with 112 CASH. The executed source differs. S12 open(90,10) funds escrow with exactly 110 CASH (invoice duty 100 = 90 + 10, reserve duty 10) and charges the buyer a separate 3 CASH opening fee, a gross debit of 113. On that source path one partial of amount a debits a + 2 and leaves 110 − a − 2 against duties of 110 − a: always 2 short (at 35: debit 37, cash 73 against duties 65 + 10 = 75). S12 checks only non-negative custody, not backing, and has no extra-funding transfer, so 112 needs a program change and a consumer-enforced backing policy. The buyer’s opening debit under the 112 design is not specified by any source. 112 backs one partial only; each further partial charges escrow another 2 that no duty reflects, so a sequence of partials needs a further funding rule. S12 has no reserve-duty-return action: after finish the source path leaves 8 against reserve duty 10 and the 112 path leaves 10 against 10, and the nonzero reserve duty blocks V2 Close on either path; discharge or migration needs a program change. Treasury. S13 allocate(true,23,7,2) needs only 23 A and 4 B for non-negative custody; holding 25 A and 10 B so that 2 A and 6 B remain is a full-backing policy a consumer must enforce. units is checked only arithmetically (23 = 3×7 + 2) and is never debited. rebate(amount) can discharge the B rebate; S13 has no action discharging allocation_reserve, so Close stays blocked. DEX, issuance and loan amounts are worked examples with no supplied source program.
technical.networkFeeNote: Cardano network fees, collateral, the min-ADA held by each proof-claim output from issuance until settlement or claimant-signed post-expiry reclaim, and the V2 thread reserve (lovelace returned on Close) are separate from the CASH amounts in the worksheet. None is estimated on this page. A program-asset fee is neither debt repayment nor a network fee, and a reserve duty is a program liability, not the thread reserve.
technical.signerBoundary: What the reviewed V2 source fixes (uncompiled-source reading): owners sign intents before proving; each intent signs per-asset gross_cap, fee_cap, net_floor and liability_cap for a beneficiary, a validity window, nonce = seq and the target predicate, VK and shape digests. Each Issue transaction carries one proof, checked by the C2 claim policy, and mints one claim output. The settlement transaction requires the signature of each claimant whose claim output it consumes and burns that output’s token. Unused claims are reclaimed with the claimant’s signature after the claimant-chosen expiry. A supplied approved=true is consented to by the effect-derived required signers, and by a listed advancer if any; that is the debited account’s consent, not a separate governance decision. The claimant is prover-chosen bytes bound at consumption, not an authenticated prover identity. Open: no transaction-by-transaction signer matrix (intent authorization, each Issue, settlement, reclaim) is published; the supplied material does not state who must sign an Issue transaction; no genuine intent signature is observed in the supplied proof records; no wallet signing display exists.
technical.readbackBoundary: Design: after submission the application separates inclusion, required finality and complete readback of outputs and remaining duties, and reconciles actual per-asset effects against the signed intents; a timeout leaves observation unknown and is not evidence of nonexecution. Status: no transaction build, submit or observe interface exists; no on-chain transaction is recorded; the acceptance and readback signal for a supported target still has to be defined and demonstrated, Preview first and later Preprod.
technical.cardsIntro: The cards below keep the reviewed role06 wording exactly. Labels such as PROPOSED, OPEN, PREMISE and V2 SOURCE READING describe the implementation status of the design explained above.

trustNotes.title: What a verifying proof shows
trustNotes.body: Under an honest setup and Groth16 knowledge soundness, a verifying proof shows the prover knew a witness satisfying the compiled constraints for its two public inputs. Linking those inputs to statement bytes additionally rests on the in-circuit BLAKE2b gadget and on BLAKE2b collision resistance. It never authenticates those bytes. A proof over supplied values does not make them an authenticated ledger fact or a true outside observation. A concrete execution proof, a universal property certificate and an authenticated ledger claim are different assertions; the latter two are not established Strand kinds.
assumptions: The current class-0 test setup is forgeable by its operator, so no production security claim follows.
Whether the compiled constraints and verifying key match your source is OPEN (T3: compiled circuit/VK and BLAKE2b gadget correspondence).
Outside facts keep their named issuer, predicate, authentication path and freshness limits.

Reference-input reads are PROPOSED: the validator must read the datum itself and authenticate its origin. PREMISE: being unspent at application shows presence only, with no exclusivity or history. A validity interval neither dates nor authenticates a datum.

SEC06-P06 PROPOSED; still needs real-context stale-sequence and expired-attestation cases, changed-reference-datum and forged-origin negatives, N5/N7–N9 at V, and a separately scoped real-context proof.
trustNotes.evidenceStage: Assumption-bound Groth16 meaning; T3 OPEN; reference-input path PROPOSED

trustNotes.title: What has actually been recorded
trustNotes.body: Evidence layers (DEMO ONLY): H ordinary host tests captured (K4H, S04; fresh actual-result review pending) | N 1 local roundtrip (S07) | V 1 local C2 wrapper, 7 cases (S08) | P none. One genuine proof was accepted by a compiled C2 wrapper in a local VM with fabricated context (S08); no on-chain transaction is recorded. S08 /cases/0 records cpu 2222340191 and mem 205312 for the whole compiled C2 Issue evaluation, including its pairing; it is neither an isolated verification cost nor ledger ExUnits, fee or transaction fit. Every recorded proof context in the supplied sources is caller-fabricated (S07, S08).
assumptions: No supplied record pins the recorded runs to the later V2 source bytes; V2 readings elsewhere on this page are not evidence about these runs.
Named runtime guards behind the six S08 rejections were not instrumented.

All 20 retained S02 families are requirements, not supported ports. The 235 catalogue IDs are pre-dedup review identifiers, not accepted or proven properties; the original 42/52 lists remain unrecovered.

Moriarty's broader target remains Midnight ZKIRv3 and native proof infrastructure; Cardano is an additional experiment and does not qualify Midnight. Preview-first and later Preprod end-to-end acceptance remain required for claimed targets.

SEC06-P08 PROPOSED (developer trust report); still needs a DEMO ONLY S07/S08 report with these qualified layers, fresh nonsecurity wording review and fresh security review. No new evidence is inferred from this layer wording.

trustNotes.title: Setup and keys
trustNotes.body: The current test setup can be forged by its operator; whether the verifying key matches the compiled relation is OPEN. Groth16 needs a separate setup per distinct compiled circuit (R1CS matrices), not per logical predicate. In the current Rust source the predicate digest is a circuit constant, so each distinct relation identity is a distinct circuit. The required total setup count is unknown; predicate, catalogue and family counts do not determine it. No production ceremony is recorded in the supplied sources, and none is proposed here.
assumptions: A future universal circuit or Midnight's universal PLONK/KZG SRS would change the comparison (PROPOSED or target-specific).

V2 SOURCE READING: catalogue VK digests are fixed at genesis and carried unchanged, and Close requires zero balances and duties, so any key change needs a PROPOSED key migration action that carries residual duties.
Intent revocation (Revoke) advances seq; it is not key migration.
SEC06-P07 PROPOSED; still needs an old-VK-refused-after-migration negative, a setup-class report and independent review of any future ceremony.
trustNotes.evidenceStage: RECORDED limitation (forgeable test setup); V2 SOURCE READING; total setup count UNKNOWN

trustNotes.title: What ties a Strand to its step
trustNotes.body: V2 SOURCE READING: tag, family, predicate_digest, shape_digest and body_len are circuit constants; the context fields vk_digest through intents_digest (bytes 112..339, including claimant_vkh) are free booleanized witness bits that are hashed, not interpreted. The consumer, not the circuit, ties those fields to the transaction: the settling validator rebuilds each statement from the transaction and the spent thread state, so a claim made for another thread step, catalogue, claimant or intent set does not match. Claimant binding happens at consumption, not at issuance: C2 Issue does not compare the claimant with the statement, so a mismatched envelope can be minted but cannot settle. This source-level binding is separate from T3, which stays OPEN.
assumptions: The class-0 setup operator can forge a proof for any digest and any claimant. The claimant is prover-chosen bytes, not an authenticated prover identity.
Builders select claim inputs; the ledger spends each claim once (PREMISE). A copied proof can be re-issued with the same claimant and a new expiry; only that claimant can release it.

Catalogue program_hash and source_hash are visible, covered by catalogue_digest and signed in every owner intent. No on-chain check links them to predicate_digest or vk_digest: that link is a CATALOGUE-AUTHOR ASSERTION and VK-to-matrix is OPEN. Exact predicate-digest field coverage depends on identity.rs, which the reviewer did not read.
The statement's network byte is declared by the catalogue and not compared with the executing ledger; separation across networks rests on outref uniqueness (PREMISE).

SEC06-P03 and SEC06-P04 PROPOSED; still need competing-claimant and same-claimant duplicate negatives, second-party source→relation→predicate reproduction, refusal-list coverage, N5/N7–N9, a T3 method, reviewed T2/T3 and F07–F10, a non-test setup, and cross-network replay analysis if the network byte is relied on.
trustNotes.evidenceStage: V2 SOURCE READING (unadopted, uncompiled); T3 OPEN

trustNotes.title: Where proofs are checked: the issuance route
trustNotes.body: In the reviewed V2 source, each proof is checked when its claim is issued: the C2 claim policy checks a Groth16 proof and mints one claim output per Issue transaction. Claims must exist before settlement. The settlement transaction consumes them, recomputes each statement and compares it with the digest checked at issuance; it does not verify the proof again. Each consumed claim needs its claimant's signature on the settlement transaction and the burn of its token. Structurally, n required Strands mean n Issue transactions plus one settlement, excluding one-time genesis and any post-expiry reclaim. These counts are readings of uncompiled source, not measurements.
assumptions: Each claim output locks min-ADA from issuance until settlement or claimant-signed reclaim after the claimant-chosen expiry. Several envelopes can exist per statement digest.

Safe but not live: any catalogue account may Revoke (advancing seq), and a competing settlement may spend the outref, orphaning issued claims and locking their value until expiry. Earlier reclaim is PROPOSED (OPEN).

Batch issuance needs a C2 change (PROPOSED). Proof-at-consumption is a different PROPOSED design needing a new redeemer and in-settlement pairings, with size and budget unmeasured. Mempool chaining is a node premise outside the sources.
V2 source already refuses two claims for one consumed outref; S09's role-level refusal is an unadopted proposal and not deduplication permission.
Owner intents are signed before proving; claimant settlement signatures are a later, distinct event. Proof collection or claim-output creation executes no effect.
Still needs orphan-after-Revoke, competing-settlement and post-expiry reclaim cases, and a qualified complete-path measurement of both verification placements.
trustNotes.evidenceStage: V2 SOURCE READING (structural); not observed onchain

trustNotes.title: Complete and incomplete Webs
trustNotes.body: PROPOSED: a Web settles only when every Strand its contract requires is present. An incomplete Web has no authority over thread effects. On the issuance route its already-issued claim outputs exist on-chain, lock value, and remain releasable only by their claimant. In the first proposed supported profile, the consumer refuses universal property certificates, authenticated-history claims, private handoff, recursive parents and multiparent joins as UNSUPPORTED; they remain required Web tracks, each needing its own trust path and evidence before any profile accepts it.
assumptions: All-or-nothing acceptance and a consumer-derived required set are PROPOSED; no Web consumer, second genuine relation or general cardinality exists in this packet.

Depicting several Strand roles does not establish separate relations or producers. A whole-execution proof may cover several claim specifications; naming source expressions fee or liability does not create independent proof producers.

A01 adopts only conditional T1: the all-role conjunction equals whole-action Core over one decoded body, modulo premise G including output well-formedness, a covering WebPlan, whole-action compilation first and the same field. There is no implementation, no T2, no T3 and no full WP migration (F07–F10); builder reliance is not permitted.
OPEN: whether a consumer can enforce a fully authorized partial financial step that carries every proof that step requires, distinct from a missing proof.

SEC06-P01 and SEC06-P02 PROPOSED; still need N1/N12 and unknown-class refusal, a report-level test that an incomplete set never renders as accepted, N1–N4/N6/N11/N14 at H/V, a wrong-action-index case, a required-set display, separate future-profile designs and fresh security review of reused V2 mechanisms.

trustNotes.title: Effects, allocation and authority
trustNotes.body: V2 SOURCE READING: owner intents sign per-asset gross_cap, fee_cap, net_floor and liability_cap for a beneficiary, a validity window, nonce = seq and the target predicate, VK and shape digests. Duties change only through recorded accruals and discharges, and a thread with a nonzero duty cannot close. The thread datum carries the complete custody snapshot, which custody must equal exactly. Actual output allocation is the consuming validator's job; a proof can attest arithmetic only over values the validator recomputes. A profile chooses either strict one-output-per-obligation or a consumer-recomputed amount partition that admits coalesced payments, with every obligation allocated exactly once.
assumptions: The source strict-output rule covers redeemers of one S2 script hash only, not other scripts or S2 versions. No input value may count toward two obligations; ledger single-spend alone is not a value partition.
Circuit-level NotBound/TouchedOnly limits remain. A general multi-UTxO authenticated frame, role sets, cross-script allocation and partial-completion rules are PROPOSED.
No genuine intent signature is observed in the supplied proof records.

A supplied approved=true is consented to by the effect-derived required signers, and by a listed advancer if any; that is the debited account's consent, not a separate governance decision. A distinct approver must be a required signer, an advancer or an authenticated input.

SEC06-P05 PROPOSED; still needs double-satisfaction negatives across scripts and S2 versions, a coalesced positive under partition, fee-over-cap and dropped-duty cases, the approver-coverage lint, a genuine validator-checked signature in real context, and independent custody/duty/backing accounting with a backing-policy negative.
trustNotes.evidenceStage: V2 SOURCE READING; allocation policy PROPOSED per profile

trustNotes.title: Duties, backing and fees
trustNotes.body: S12 and S13 source behavior requires non-negative custody, not full backing of liabilities. S12 funds escrow at 110: partial(35) debits 37 and leaves 73 against duties of 75 (invoice 65, reserve 10), which is 2 short. Funding 112 would back one partial; each further partial charges another 2 that no duty reflects. That backing is a PROPOSED application policy. S12 has no extra transfer and no reserve-duty-return action; after finish, escrow holds 8 against reserve duty 10, and the nonzero reserve duty blocks V2 Close. S13 allocate(true,23,7,2) needs at least 23 A and 4 B for non-negative custody; 25 A and 10 B is PROPOSED full backing, and S13 has no action discharging allocation_reserve.
assumptions: Source-only arithmetic, not execution. The V2 Close zero-duty condition is an uncompiled-source reading.
Even under the proposed 112 policy the reserve duty stays 10 and Close stays blocked; discharge or migration needs a program change.
S13 units is checked only arithmetically (23 = 3×7 + 2) and is never debited.

A program-asset fee is not debt repayment and not a network fee. Network fees, collateral, claim-output min-ADA and the V2 thread reserve (lovelace returned on Close) are separate funding items; a reserve duty is a program liability.
Delivery evidence and dispute rules remain named assumptions. Still needs independent open/partial/finish/reserve-return accounting and a backing-policy negative.
trustNotes.evidenceStage: Source arithmetic reading; full backing PROPOSED

trustNotes.title: What the interactive page does
trustNotes.body: The invoice worksheet is local browser arithmetic over the S12 fixture values; it does not execute Moriarty, produce or check a proof, or create a transaction or ledger state. The explorer’s remove and restore control shows the consumer rule; a complete Web on this page is not proof verification, acceptance or settlement. Role cards state what each transition must prove; they do not claim fifteen independently implemented proof producers, and the supplied proof evidence concerns one invoice-partial relation. DEX, issuance and loan amounts are worked examples with no supplied source program; issuance additionally needs an application mint policy, which is distinct from the C2 claim policy. Identifiers shown in the explorer are placeholders. Cost: more Strands can duplicate context hashing, range constraints, exports, issuance and verification, and whole execution may be preferable; no measurement exists.

trustNotes.title: Permissionless use and retained scope
trustNotes.body: Moriarty is a permissionless language of provable intention: any developer may author, compile, prove, publish and deploy programs in the supported language without approval from Moriarty maintainers, an agent council, Foreman, a hosted solver or a program registry. Objective validity rules, resource costs and asset-owner authorization still apply, and application-specific access control remains expressible without becoming a deployment restriction. Optional hosted proving, relaying or indexing services are never required. Moriarty's broader target remains Midnight ZKIRv3 and native proof infrastructure; Cardano is an additional experiment and does not replace that contract or qualify Midnight. Preview-first and later Preprod end-to-end acceptance remain required for claimed targets. No claim is made that a Cardano Web ports to another target unchanged.

groth16.title: Groth16 proofs and trusted setup
groth16.intro: Groth16 lets a prover show that a computation satisfies a fixed set of constraints without publishing its private inputs. A Strand uses it to carry a compact proof that the financial calculation follows those rules. Here is what the proof contains, what the validator checks and why setup is needed.

concepts.label: Public information
concepts.title: The statement
concepts.body: The statement says what is being proved. In a Web, the public inputs carry a digest of the statement bytes. The validator rebuilds those bytes from the transaction, so a correct calculation cannot be attached to a different payment. A proof alone does not authenticate an external price or document.

concepts.label: Private information
concepts.title: The witness
concepts.body: The witness contains the other values needed to satisfy the circuit, including intermediate calculations. The proof hides those values. Anything already published in a Cardano output or the public statement remains public.

concepts.label: The check
concepts.title: Proof and verification key
concepts.body: The proving key lets a prover create a proof from the statement and witness. The validator uses the verification key and public inputs to check a proof of three group elements with a pairing equation. Both keys are public; the secret that must be destroyed belongs to setup.

groth16.setupTitle: Why there is a trusted setup
groth16.setupIntro: Groth16 needs parameters for the exact compiled circuit. Setup derives the proving and verification keys using secret randomness. If someone retains that randomness, they can forge proofs. A common ceremony divides this work into two phases so part of it can be shared.

setupStages.label: Phase 1
setupStages.title: Parameters that circuits can share
setupStages.body: Often called powers of tau, this phase prepares parameters for a particular curve and capacity. Circuits can reuse them when their curve and format are compatible and they fit within that capacity.

setupStages.label: Phase 2
setupStages.title: Keys for one compiled circuit
setupStages.body: Each distinct circuit needs its own second phase. Its constraints, public-input layout and bounds determine which keys are valid. New values can reuse those keys; a changed circuit needs a new phase 2.

counter.title: How many setup stages are needed?
counter.body: Assume these circuits share a compatible curve and format, and one phase-1 parameter set is large enough for all of them. Change the count to see what can be reused.
counter.label: Distinct compiled circuits
counter.result: For {K} distinct circuits, phase 1 can be shared and phase 2 runs {K} times. These are stages, not {K} + 1 complete ceremonies.
counter.conditions: The count holds only if every circuit uses the same curve and format and fits the shared phase-1 capacity. Smaller circuits need no extra phase 1. Each stage yields sound keys only if its transcript verifies and at least one participant in it was honest.

groth16.reuseTitle: When can the same keys be used again?

reuseExamples.title: The amounts or users change
reuseExamples.body: The keys can be reused if the compiled circuit stays the same. New transactions and different public-input values do not, by themselves, require setup again.

reuseExamples.title: The compiled rules change
reuseExamples.body: A circuit with different constraints, bounds or public-input layout needs a new phase 2. A new Groth16 wrapper also has its own circuit. Aggregation does not remove setup for the base circuits.

reuseExamples.title: One bounded circuit covers several kinds of claim
reuseExamples.body: A parameterized circuit can cover many claims within fixed bounds. That is how a catalogue can contain more claim types than circuits. It does not make the circuit unbounded.

groth16.trust: Proving and verification keys are public. The secret is the setup randomness, often called toxic waste. Anyone who holds it can produce verifying proofs for statements that have no witness, so it must not survive the setup. A multi-party phase is trustworthy when its transcript verifies and at least one participant in that phase was honest, under the protocol's assumptions. Every phase needs that property.
groth16.cardanoTitle: How many setups for all of Cardano?
groth16.cardanoCount: There is no fixed Cardano-wide total. Count one phase 2 for each distinct compiled circuit, including wrappers. Count phase 1 separately for each compatible parameter set those circuits use; an existing set can be reused if its capacity is sufficient. Claim types and architectural layers do not determine the number of circuits. A total requires a frozen inventory of compiled circuits.

sevenLayers.title: The parts of a zero-knowledge proof system
sevenLayers.intro: A proof is useful only if it checks the right program against the right inputs. These seven concerns explain the connection, from the financial rules a developer writes to the checks a Cardano validator performs. They influence one another; the numbers are not seven execution steps.
sevenLayers.selectorLabel: Choose a part of the proof system

layers.name: Setup
layers.headline: Which keys does the circuit use?
layers.body: Groth16 derives proving and verifying keys from secret randomness for one compiled circuit. Each distinct compiled relation needs its own phase-2 setup; the count follows circuits, not predicates or catalogue entries. Whoever keeps that randomness can forge proofs, so soundness assumes it is destroyed.
layers.mapping: Catalogue entries and owner intents name the verifying key.
layers.subtitle: Keys for the compiled circuit

layers.name: Language
layers.headline: What rules does the contract enforce?
layers.body: Moriarty programs state what an action may do: payment arithmetic, fees kept separate from repayment, caps an owner signs, and duties that continue. The compiler turns that source into constraints; a rule left unconstrained is a rule no proof enforces.
layers.mapping: Moriarty rules for payments, fees, caps and duties.
layers.subtitle: The financial program

layers.name: Witness
layers.headline: Which values satisfy those rules?
layers.body: The prover runs the program over its inputs and records every intermediate value. Zero-knowledge keeps this assignment hidden, but only the assignment: amounts that appear in Cardano outputs or in the statement stay public. Witness generation must not leak values through its own behavior.
layers.mapping: One whole-execution witness can serve several Strand roles.
layers.subtitle: The prover’s private inputs

layers.name: Arithmetization
layers.headline: How are the rules expressed as constraints?
layers.body: The compiled program becomes rank-1 constraints over a prime field, which Groth16 encodes as a quadratic arithmetic program. A valid witness satisfies every constraint. The public inputs carry a statement digest; an in-circuit BLAKE2b gadget ties them to the statement bytes.
layers.mapping: Caps, fees and duty updates become constraints.
layers.subtitle: Equations the proof can check
layers.plainLanguage: The compiler translates the program into equations. A prover must supply values that satisfy all of them. Arithmetization is the name for this way of expressing the computation.

layers.name: Proof System
layers.headline: How does Groth16 prove the calculation?
layers.body: Groth16 turns the witness into a constant-size proof checked by one pairing equation. Under an honest setup, knowledge soundness means a verifying proof shows the prover knew a satisfying witness; zero-knowledge means the proof reveals nothing beyond its statement. It never shows the statement's values describe the real ledger.
layers.subtitle: The proof construction

layers.name: Cryptographic Bedrock
layers.headline: Which cryptographic assumptions does it rely on?
layers.body: A pairing-friendly elliptic curve supplies Groth16's groups and scalar field; Groth16's soundness argument holds in the generic bilinear group model. BLAKE2b collision resistance binds statement bytes to digests. Signatures authenticate owner intents and claimant releases. These primitives support the proof core and fix what it can express.
layers.mapping: Cardano scripts evaluate the pairing check and hashes.
layers.subtitle: Curves, hashes and signatures

layers.name: Verification
layers.headline: Does this proof belong to this transaction?
layers.body: A claim policy checks each Groth16 proof and mints a proof-claim output. One settlement transaction consumes the proof-claim output of every Strand the Web requires; the validator rebuilds each statement from the transaction and spent state, requires claimant signatures and enforces signed caps. Outside facts need a named issuer, authentication path and freshness limit.
layers.subtitle: The connection to Cardano

sevenLayers.relationshipsTitle: How these concerns affect one another
relationships: Layers 4, 5 and 6 form the proof core: the scalar field, the R1CS encoding and Groth16's pairing check are chosen as one design, not three.
Setup follows the compiled relation. Changing a rule changes the circuit, and a changed circuit needs a new setup and a new verifying key.
The proof and the ledger divide the work. Layers 3 to 5 show the statement's arithmetic is correct; Layer 7 checks, from the transaction itself, that the statement describes this step.
The verifier reaches down. Cardano scripts must run the pairing check, which constrains the curve and proof system beneath them.
The numbering follows how a reader meets the system, not the order of engineering decisions; the dependency lists here sketch the main pressures, not a complete graph.
